purpose: Harden the GitHub Actions release adapter so registry publication and repository mutation occur only through a narrowly authorized, reviewable release boundary.
scope: .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml and its referenced actions, GitHub Environment configuration documentation, action pinning, permissions, artifact handoff, and workflow tests. The non_goal below of not making GitHub Actions the only supported CI/release platform refers to the portability of the callisto CLI as a build tool; it does not constrain the mechanisms this repository's own meta-release pipeline may use. A GitHub-Environment-specific protection gate on this repo's release workflow (AC-001) is in scope and does not conflict with that non-goal. This spec declares its build dependencies explicitly in depends_on. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001 owns the plan-job to execute-job topology and the durable-plan envelope schema and upload/download flow; neither exists in the current workflow, where a single `release` job invokes the composite callisto-action and computes the plan inline (`callisto plan-publish`) in the same shell block that pushes tags and creates the GitHub release. AC-001 and AC-006 consume that topology and that envelope rather than defining them, and must therefore be sequenced after SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001 ships. SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002 owns source_commit resolution and the structured HEAD-vs-source_commit mismatch error that AC-006's validation step matches on.
non_goals: Making GitHub Actions the only supported CI or release platform.
Moving provider-neutral release rules from callisto core into workflow shell code.
Requiring Git tag signing in this track; signature policy is covered by SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002.

Defining the plan/execute job topology or the durable-plan envelope schema. Both are owned by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001; this spec consumes them and adds the authorization, pinning, permission, and review boundary around the execute job.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The workflow's current single `release` job (which today computes the plan and performs tag/publish/gh-release in one shell script) is split into two jobs per the plan-job to execute-job topology defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001: an unprivileged planning job with no registry secrets and a read-only or no GITHUB_TOKEN, and a separate privileged execution job that performs tag/publish/release actions. The execution job is bound to a GitHub Environment (`environment:` key referencing a named environment such as `release`) that has required reviewers and branch/tag deployment rules configured. The repository documents that environment's name, its required reviewers, its branch/tag deployment rules, and an administrator-verifiable API or console procedure for confirming those rules are actually configured on the repository. The workflow YAML `environment:` reference alone is explicitly insufficient evidence that protection rules exist: the key declares intent, and GitHub auto-creates a referenced environment with zero protection rules on first use unless required reviewers have been separately configured via repo Settings. This criterion owns the topology and the documented procedure; AC-004 owns the automated enforcement that the documented rules are live. Non-release jobs (verify, planning) receive neither registry secrets nor write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN permissions.

Each workflow and job declares the least GitHub token permissions it needs. contents, pull-requests, checks, and statuses are write-scoped only in the job that demonstrably performs that operation; all other jobs default to read or none. A workflow test or policy check rejects an unscoped top-level write grant.
Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable full commit SHAs (40 hex characters), each with a nearby comment recording the upstream tag or release used, for human review.
CI verifies every external action reference's pin format and fails the build if any external action reference is changed to a mutable tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA.

A CI or setup check calls the GitHub API (e.g. `gh api repos/{repo}/environments/{name}`) against the environment named in AC-001's `environment:` key and fails unless that environment's `protection_rules` array contains an entry with `"type": "required_reviewers"` and a non-empty `reviewers` list. A non-empty `protection_rules` array is not by itself sufficient: live GitHub data confirms environments commonly carry only a `branch_policy` rule (restricts which branch may deploy) with no human approval gate at all -- that shape must still fail this check. This check is the automated enforcement of AC-001's evidentiary rule, and it must read live environment configuration through the API rather than inspecting workflow YAML, so that a diff which merely adds `environment: release` can never by itself satisfy it.

The planning job (per AC-001) uploads the explicit durable plan defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001 as a build artifact. The privileged execution job downloads only that artifact from its own workflow run, verifies its source_commit against its own checkout per SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002 AC-002, and fails before any registry or repository credentials are used if validation fails, surfacing that spec's structured mismatch error rather than a free-text-only diagnostic. Caches may accelerate dependency installation but are never read as release intent. Implementation of this criterion is blocked on SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001 shipping its artifact schema and upload/download flow first; see depends_on and the scope note on sequencing.

Changes to files under `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/` require review from a designated set of owners before merge, enforced via CODEOWNERS combined with a branch protection rule requiring that review on those paths. This is distinct from and in addition to AC-001's environment gate: the environment gate controls who can trigger a *deployment* from an already-merged workflow, while this criterion controls who can *merge changes* to the workflow/action definitions that determine what a future deployment does.

implementation_notes: AC-004b (SHA-pin drift detection): consider adopting the maintained `step-security/github-actions-ensure-sha-pinned-actions` GitHub Action rather than hand-rolling the check -- it is the actively maintained successor to the now-stale `zgosalvez/github-actions-ensure-sha-pinned-actions`. Whichever is adopted must itself be pinned to a commit SHA, or it reintroduces the exact circular-trust problem AC-003 targets.

AC-003/AC-004b/AC-004 are pure GitHub Actions YAML/CLI concerns -- stay with `gh api` and shell, consistent with callisto-action's existing pattern (action.yml already shells to `gh` for every GitHub interaction). No Rust crate (e.g. octocrab) is warranted for this narrow, workflow-scoped check.
